name: Autosomal Dominant Isolated Diffuse Palmoplantar Keratoderma

criteria.description: Presence of diffuse thickening of the skin on the palms and soles
Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Lack of additional ectodermal or systemic abnormalities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Diffuse palmoplantar keratoderma with autosomal dominant inheritance and absence of syndromic features
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by family history and exclusion of syndromic keratodermas

laboratory: Skin biopsy showing marked hyperkeratosis with preserved epidermal architecture
Negative fungal cultures to exclude tinea
genetic: Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with keratinocyte differentiation (e.g., KRT1, KRT9) in some cases
other: Family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of associated ectodermal or systemic abnormalities
Additional features such as hearing loss, cardiomyopathy, or hair abnormalities

redFlags: Rapid progression of keratoderma with ulceration
Presence of systemic symptoms such as hearing loss or cardiac abnormalities
